title: The Machine That Makes You Happy
question: Do you want to be happy, or do you want it to be true?

lines.say: [softly] Imagine a machine... that could give you a perfect life.
[thoughtful] Every dream. Every success. Every love. [pause] All of it... perfectly felt.
[softly] There's only one thing. [pause] None of it would be real.
[calm] On one side, a life where nothing ever goes wrong. [pause] On the other... a life that rains. That hurts. That's true.
[thoughtful] Here, every smile is guaranteed. [pause] There, every smile is earned... [pause] or maybe just lucky.
[softly] And if you could never tell the difference... [pause] would it matter?
[whispers] Do you want to be happy... [pause] or do you want it to be true?

music_prompt: Intimate solo felt piano, slow and contemplative, gentle and ambiguous, neither happy nor sad, a hint of music-box celesta like a dream. Sparse notes, lots of space, soft room reverb, airy pad underneath. Starts with one high note, two alternating themes: one warm and golden, one cooler and rainy, then a near-silent pause around 44-47 seconds, ending on an unresolved suspended chord that rings out. No drums, no vocals.
